Help_Overview_Intro: WhisperLoom turns speech into text: you dictate, the app recognises the text, improves it with a stage if you like and inserts it. Pick a topic on the left or search. F1 opens the matching help in every window.
Help_company_Body:
## Connecting
• Settings → Company → “Connect to company …” or “With my company” in the wizard.
• You get the server address (https://…) and the company code (16 characters, e.g. ABCD-EFGH-JKMN-PQRS) from your IT. You can simply click an invitation link (whisperloom://join…).
• The device then waits for approval in the IT portal; the app continues by itself.
## What changes
• Fixed settings are hidden and the page shows “Some settings are managed by …”. Defaults carry the label “Company default”; you may change them and reset them.
• Your own hotkeys always stay free.
• Sync every 15 minutes or right away with “Sync now”. If the server is unreachable, the last configuration keeps applying.
## Leaving
• “Leave company …” removes the connection; the company values stay as your own settings. Some companies do not allow this.
Help_company_Intro: If your company runs its own WhisperLoom server, IT manages providers, models and access for you. You only need the server address and a company code.
Help_dictation_Body:
## Hold (default Ctrl+Win)
• Hold the keys, speak, release. The text lands in the window that was active when you started.
## Toggle (default Ctrl+Space)
• Press once to open the overlay with level and time. Press again or Enter to insert, Backspace discards.
• In the overlay you can click the stage for this one dictation.
• To press Enter after inserting (e.g. to send in a chat), turn on “Press Enter after inserting” under Output or set it per app profile (Default, On, Off).
## While the text is being improved
• Pressing the shortcut again (hold or toggle) starts the next dictation right away. The current one is still improved and inserted; results arrive in dictation order, each in its own window.
• Double-press (twice within 0.4 s) or Esc: insert now without AI, no new recording starts. Linux: run “WhisperLoom toggle” twice in quick succession.
## Without hotkeys
• Tray menu → Start/Stop recording, or the stage view (click the tray icon) with start, pause and stage.
• Linux: bind a desktop shortcut to “WhisperLoom toggle”; the result is then on the clipboard.
## Long dictations
• With online recognition a notice appears after 10 minutes and recording stops by itself after 12 minutes (provider limit). Local recognition has no limit.
## Stage view
• Shows raw text and result side by side in large type, e.g. for a projector. Font size: Settings → Dictation → Stage.
Help_dictation_Intro: On Windows you dictate into any program with a hotkey: Hold records while the keys are pressed; Toggle opens a small overlay and a second press sends.
Help_history_Body:
• Open: tray menu → History. Entries are grouped by day; search (Ctrl+F) looks through all texts.
• Keys: Enter inserts, Ctrl+C copies, F2 edits, Del deletes, Ctrl+Z brings deleted entries back.
• Reprocess recomputes from the origin (raw text) with another stage – as a new version in the background, without audio.
• The last 10 dictations are also in the tray menu under “Recent dictations”; a click inserts or copies.
• Text only, never audio. Turn off or change the size: Settings → Privacy. Turning it off deletes all entries.
Help_history_Intro: History keeps your recent dictations as text – to insert again, copy, edit or reprocess with another stage.
Help_hotkeys_Body:
## Defaults (Windows)
• Hold: Ctrl+Win – records while pressed.
• Toggle: Ctrl+Space – opens the overlay, a second press sends.
• Next stage: Ctrl+Alt+Space.
• Insert last dictation again: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V.
• Process selection: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S.
## Changing
• Settings → Dictation → Shortcuts → “Change …”, then press the new combination (Esc cancels).
• Warnings below the row name conflicts, e.g. Ctrl+Alt = AltGr (blocks special characters) or combinations Windows uses itself.
• “Global hotkeys on” switches all of them off and on at once.
## Linux
• Wayland does not allow global hotkeys for apps. In GNOME or KDE, bind your own shortcuts to “WhisperLoom toggle”, “WhisperLoom stage next” and “WhisperLoom process-selection”.
Help_hotkeys_Intro: All hotkeys can be changed and work in every program. They stay yours even when a company manages the app.
Help_it_Body:
## Three levels per setting
• Fixed: set centrally and hidden in the app; the page shows “Some settings are managed by …”.
• Default: preset centrally; users may change it and reset it to the company default.
• Free: nothing central. Hotkeys are never fixed.
## Company server
• Folder server/ in the repository (Docker or systemd): tenants, company codes and invitation links, device approval in the portal, policy, provider keys encrypted on the server, proxy mode without keys on the devices, usage statistics and budget limits. When the budget is reached, devices get a clear message – no fallback provider, no switching to local.
• Portal sign-in: two-factor (TOTP) is optional; on first login the setup can be skipped with “Set up later”. To require two-factor for all admins, allow only “Password and two-factor” on the “Company” page.
## Provisioning file
• A JSON file with providers, keys, locked fields, history and updates, e.g. via logon script or Intune; format in docs/settings-format.md.
## Distribution and operation
• Per-user setup without admin rights or portable ZIP; updates can be turned off by policy (updatesEnabled=false); signing by the company: docs/signing.md.
• Proxy: system including PAC and NTLM/Kerberos. Logs contain only metadata, audio never touches the disk.
Help_it_Intro: Summary for administrators: WhisperLoom can be managed centrally through your own company server or a provisioning file – both work the same way.
Help_network_Body:
• System: on Windows, uses the user's proxy setting including PAC script and sign-in with your Windows account (NTLM/Kerberos); on Linux, reads the environment variables (HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY).
• Manual: your own address, e.g. http://proxy:3128.
• Off: straight to the internet, without proxy.
• Ollama and the bundled local services on 127.0.0.1 never go through the proxy. For your own servers in the LAN, set NO_PROXY or the system proxy exceptions if needed.
• Error “Server unreachable”? Check network and proxy first, then “Send again” in the tray.
Help_network_Intro: In company networks the way to the internet often goes through a proxy. By default WhisperLoom uses the system one.
Help_output_Body:
## Windows
• Output result: Paste (the clipboard is restored afterwards), Type directly or Clipboard only.
• “Always copy to the clipboard too” also puts the text there.
• “Press Enter after inserting”, e.g. to send in a chat.
• App profiles: if the target window matches a profile (program, optional window title), its stage, output and Enter apply. A button adds suggestions for Terminal and Outlook.
## When inserting fails
• No input field, target window gone or an admin window: the text is on the clipboard and a notice says so – paste with Ctrl+V.
## Password fields
• Recognised password fields never receive text: nothing is inserted, nothing goes to the clipboard or history.
• In browsers and WebView2 or Electron apps (e.g. Teams, Slack, VS Code) fields often cannot be recognised. There WhisperLoom still inserts and then restores the previous clipboard – so take care when dictating into web password fields.
## Linux
• The result of every dictation is on the clipboard (install wl-clipboard or xclip). Paste with Ctrl+V.
## Once more
• Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V inserts the last dictation again, Linux: “WhisperLoom reinsert”.
Help_output_Intro: Where the text goes after dictation: on Windows straight into the active program, on Linux to the clipboard.
Help_privacy_Body:
• Audio never touches the disk. It only stays in memory until recognition is done or while “Send again” is possible.
• API keys are stored in the system keychain (Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service or a file with permissions 600) – never in the settings, never in an export, never in the log. The interface always masks them.
• History: text only, can be turned off. Turning it off deletes all entries, shrinking deletes the oldest.
• Logs only contain metadata (duration, provider, status, error class) – never dictated text.
• Online recognition sends the audio to the chosen provider; with local recognition and a local text model everything stays on the PC.
• Recognised password fields never receive text (not on the clipboard or in history either), and the floating button does not appear there. In browsers and WebView2 or Electron apps password fields often cannot be recognised: there the text is inserted and the previous clipboard restored afterwards.
Help_privacy_Intro: What WhisperLoom stores and what it never stores: audio stays in memory, keys in the keychain, dictations only in history – if you want.
Help_providers_Body:
## Custom providers
• Settings → Connections → Custom providers → Add provider: name, address, protocol (OpenAI-compatible, Ollama, ElevenLabs, Anthropic) and key.
• The provider can then be chosen in every slot – recognition, text and fallback.
## Local Whisper models
• Settings → Recognition → Local recognition: choose, download, pause and delete models.
• Your own file: “Add file …” there – a ggml or gguf file, e.g. a fine-tuned model.
## Local text models and servers
• Bundled text model via llama.cpp: download once; it starts when needed, even while you are still recording.
• Ollama: install it, pull a model (e.g. “ollama pull qwen3:4b”), then choose it under Text → With local recognition.
• Your own servers (LM Studio, llama.cpp, faster-whisper-server) go under Connections → Local servers; afterwards they can be chosen as providers, also in the fallback chain.
Help_providers_Intro: Besides the built-in providers you can add your own services, your own Whisper files and local servers.
Help_recognition_Body:
## Online
• Settings → Recognition → Online: choose a provider (e.g. OpenAI, Groq, Mistral, ElevenLabs or your own), enter your key, leave the model empty for the recommendation.
• The key is stored in the system keychain and masked everywhere.
• Fallback provider: steps in when the first one fails.
## Local
• Recognition → Local recognition, then download a model there. Bigger = more accurate but slower; “Accurate recognition” works even harder.
• Compute: graphics card (Vulkan), CPU on error – or CPU only.
## Recognise better
• Set the dictation language instead of automatic. For German dictations with English terms there is “German + English” (online works best with GPT Transcribe; the local model recognises only one language per dictation).
• Context words: names and technical terms, one entry per line, or as a file.
Help_recognition_Intro: Online, a provider of your choice recognises with your key – fast and accurate. Locally, whisper.cpp runs on this PC without internet.
Help_selection_Body:
## Starting (Windows)
• Hotkey, default Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S: opens the stage picker at the text cursor.
• Floating button (off by default, turn on under Dictation → Process selected text): after selecting with the mouse, “Process” briefly appears next to it – never in password fields, can be turned off per app profile.
• Ctrl+right-click (off by default, turn on in the same place) on a selection opens the picker; without a selection you get the normal context menu.
• Always available: tray menu → Process selection …
## In the picker
• ↑/↓ to choose, 1–9 directly, Enter processes, Esc cancels.
• “Rewrite by instruction …” records a spoken instruction, e.g. “turn this into a polite refusal”.
• The result replaces the selection. If the target window no longer fits, it is on the clipboard; if something fails, the selection stays unchanged.
## Linux
• Select text, then run “WhisperLoom process-selection” from a shortcut (with “--stage beautify” to skip the choice). The result is on the clipboard; needs wl-clipboard or xclip.
Help_selection_Intro: Edit selected text in any program with a stage – polish, beautify, summarize or rewrite it by spoken instruction.
Help_stages_Body:
## The stages
• Off: the recognised raw text, only cleaned up (fillers, capitalisation).
• Polish: grammar and punctuation, the content stays. “Polish: cleanup” sets how much may change, up to “Readable” (gentle copy-editing).
• Beautify: smoother style, with paragraphs if you like.
• Summarize: the essentials in brief, as prose or bullet points.
• Prompt: turns the dictation into a clear prompt for AI assistants (switch it on under Text → Stage).
## Switching
• Tray menu → Stage, the “Next stage” hotkey (default Ctrl+Alt+Space) or the command “WhisperLoom stage next”.
• App profiles set a stage per program (Settings → Output).
## Who improves the text?
• The AI provider under “Text”; “Same as recognition” uses the recognition provider and key.
• With local recognition, “Text improvement with local recognition” decides: “Local on this PC” (Ollama, bundled model or your own server), “Online, otherwise local” or “Online, otherwise without AI”.
• If text improvement is unreachable, WhisperLoom inserts the raw text and tells you.
• Cleanup: remove fillers (uh, um …), add your own, keep single ones, capitalise sentence starts.
Help_stages_Intro: The stage decides what happens to the text after recognition – from unchanged raw text to a finished prompt.
Help_start_Body:
## Setup
• On first start the wizard asks: for you or with your company, language, microphone with level test, recognition, stage, hotkeys and autostart.
• You can skip at any time. Open it again: Settings → System → Setup or the command “WhisperLoom setup”.
• If your IT has fixed some settings, those steps are skipped.
## Where to find what
• Tray menu: start recording, switch stage, recent dictations, process selection, history, stage view, settings and help.
• Settings in seven pages by task: Dictation (shortcuts, microphone, selection, stage), Recognition, Text, Output, Connections, Privacy, System (interface language, updates, export and import – compatible with the Android app, keys are never exported – and setup); plus “Company” at the end of the sidebar.
• Help: F1 in every window or the help button next to the title of every settings page.
Help_start_Intro: WhisperLoom runs in the background with an icon in the notification area. The setup wizard takes you to your first dictation in a few steps.
Help_trouble_Body:
## No usable microphone
• Settings → Dictation → choose the microphone; check the connection. Windows: Privacy → Microphone → allow desktop apps.
## Recognition not set up
• Enter a provider and key under Recognition, or switch to Local and download a model.
## Server unreachable
• Check internet and proxy (Settings → Connections → Proxy). While the audio is still in memory, tray menu → “Send again” retries. A fallback provider helps during outages.
## Server reports an error
• Usually the key is invalid, the credit used up or the model wrong: replace the key, leave the model empty (recommendation).
## Local recognition not ready
• Download a model under Recognition → Local recognition or check your own file; try “CPU only” as compute.
## Inserted without AI
• Text improvement was unreachable: check provider and key under “Text”; with Ollama: is the service running?
## Text is on the clipboard instead of in the program
• No input field, target window gone or admin window: paste with Ctrl+V. Recognised password fields never receive text (“Password field – not inserted”).
## Output to the clipboard failed
• Another program is holding the clipboard right now. Wait a moment and copy the dictation again from history or tray menu → Recent dictations.
## Hotkeys do nothing
• Settings → Dictation → Shortcuts: is “Global hotkeys on” set? Mind the conflict warnings. Linux: set up desktop shortcuts.
## Company
• “Company budget reached for this month”: the request is clearly refused, without fallback provider and without switching to local – contact your IT. “Device blocked”: also your IT. Company server unreachable: the last configuration keeps applying.
Help_trouble_Intro: The most common messages and what helps. The message appears in the overlay, on the stage view or as a notice near the tray.
History_ClearConfirm: Delete all {0} dictations? This cannot be undone.
History_OffConfirm_Desc: Turning it off deletes all saved dictations. This cannot be undone.

History_Status_copyFailed: Copying did not work – the clipboard is busy. Try again in a moment.
History_Status_done: Processed again – result is on the clipboard
History_Status_insertFailed: Inserting did not work. The text is on the clipboard – paste it with Ctrl+V.
History_Status_kept: The version was edited meanwhile – the edit stays
Hotkey_Conflict_AltGr: Ctrl+Alt is AltGr: blocks special characters
Hotkey_Conflict_Autocomplete: Used by VS Code and IntelliJ (autocomplete)
Hotkey_Conflict_InputLanguage: Windows uses it to switch the input language

Hotkey_Conflict_SingleModifier: A single modifier interferes with normal typing
Hotkey_Conflict_Windows: Win combinations are often taken by Windows
Hotkey_Recording: Press the new key combination now … Esc cancels
Insert_InputRejected: Input rejected – text is on the clipboard
Insert_NoTextField: No text field – text is on the clipboard
Insert_NotForeground: Target window not reachable – text is on the clipboard
Insert_TargetGone: Target window is gone – text is on the clipboard

Key_AtCompany: Runs through your company: this device signs in to the company server itself, no key of your own is needed.
Key_AtEntry: The key belongs to the provider (page “Connections”) and is only sent to its address.
Language_deEnHint: For German dictation with English words. GPT Transcribe gets both languages as a hint, all other services detect the language themselves.
Language_deEnOffline: The local model detects only one language per dictation. English words in a German dictation may be misspelled.
Local_BundledHint: Download the model from the list above. It starts on demand, already while you record.
Local_ModelsMoved: Download models and add your own Whisper files in the list above.

Local_OllamaMissing: Ollama not found (127.0.0.1:11434). Install and start it, then reload:
Local_SelectedFileMissing: The chosen file is missing or is not a model. Choose another model or add the file again.
Local_ServerHint: Add servers on the page “Connections” › Local servers.
Models_Http: The server refused the model list request. Check the address and key.
Models_NoAccess: “Same as recognition” has no access with local recognition.
Models_NoList: The server returned no model list.
Next_PendingHint: Previous dictation is still being improved and will be inserted next · Esc = insert now without AI
Output_Hint_RawOnly: Inserted without AI – text improvement not reachable
Output_LinuxHint: On Linux the result of every dictation is on the clipboard. Paste with Ctrl+V.
Overlay_StageTip: Choose the stage for this dictation
Policy_Hint: Greyed-out fields are set by IT.
Profile_InvalidTitle: WhisperLoom can’t read this expression, so the profile doesn’t apply like this. Check brackets and characters such as ( ) [ ] \ |.
Provider_InUse: In use by: {0}. Choose another provider there first.
Provider_KeyNewHost: The stored key will now be sent to {0}. Keep it only if you trust this server; otherwise delete the key.
Provider_Key_Desc: Belongs to this provider and is only sent to its address.
Provider_Models_Desc: Model IDs, comma-separated. Empty = load the list from the server.
Provider_Protocol_Desc: OpenAI-compatible: recognition and text. Ollama, Anthropic: text. ElevenLabs: recognition.
Providers_DeleteConfirm: Delete the provider and its key? Recognition, text and fallback that use it fall back to the default. This cannot be undone.
Providers_Empty: No custom providers yet. The built-in ones only need an API key.
Recording_Capped: 12 minutes reached – recording paused; send it now

Rewrite_NoInstruction: No instruction recognised – selection left unchanged
Rewrite_RestoreFailed: Clipboard could not be restored – it now holds the selection

Server_NameInvalid: Name missing, contains “:” or is already used. Not saved.

Set_AlwaysCopy: Always copy to the clipboard too
Set_AlwaysCopy_Desc: After inserting, the text is also on the clipboard. Without a text field it always goes there.
Set_ApiKey_Desc: Stored in the system keychain, never in the settings file
Set_CtrlRightClick_Desc: Ctrl+right-click on a selection opens the stage picker; without a selection the normal context menu appears
Set_CustomModels_Desc: A ggml or gguf file, for example a fine-tuned model; it appears in the list above.
Set_CustomProviders_Desc: Selectable for every access: recognition, text and fallback.

Set_Engine_Desc: Online: provider with API key. Local: whisper.cpp on this PC.
Set_FallbackEnabled_Desc: Steps in when the first provider fails

Set_HistoryEnabled_Desc: Text only, no audio. Turning it off deletes the history.
Set_InsertMode_Desc: Applies to hold and toggle; app profiles can change it per app
